facts.text: Sterling was officially platted in 1880, marking its formal recognition as a community within Wayne County.
The town’s roots trace back to 1817 when settlers from Pennsylvania and New York cleared Milton Township’s forests for farming.
Early Sterling boasted grist mills, grain warehouses, and veterinary practices, all thanks to its proximity to the railroads that linked the area to larger markets.
Sterling sits at 40°57′58″N 81°50′38″W, just 10 miles northwest of Wooster, and rises 968 feet above sea level.
The community’s climate is humid continental, with average annual temperatures around 52°F and about 40 inches of yearly rainfall.
Sterling’s landscape is dominated by fertile yellow clayey soils, ideal for the cattle and crop farming that still define the area today.
